summary: Turn 11. All previously raised Candidates are accepted as explained and pending_work was empty, so I widened the search into the previously unread A7 client path. Sourced finding (recorded, not claimed as a defect): in client/buffer.go, WaitReplies decodes each ProposeReplyTS and forwards its CommandId to RegisterReply, so reply identity exists, but RegisterReply discards it and the Loop consumer reads c.Reply purely in arrival order — it advances one counter per reply and the blocking Write/Read/Scan helpers take whichever reply arrives first (client/buffer.go:68-72 and 92-200), with the source's own TODO 'if the return value != i, something's wrong'. Because the map had no client Behavior or Fact, I recorded this as an unclassified sourced Surface ('client.BufferClient reply correlation (WaitReplies / RegisterReply / Loop)', disposition UNCLASSIFIED_PROTOCOL_RESPONSIBILITY) with a new range S-CLIENT-REPLY over client/buffer.go:60-200, rather than inventing A7 Behavior/Fact objects or an obligation. The submitted product is action=research with map_path=map.json (base version 2, corrected from 1 after the validator reported the accepted base) plus feedback referencing the new material. Remaining keeps the contract questions explicit: whether the client contract requires request-to-reply identity, whether the pipelined window can deliver replies out of order in this protocol, and whether to promote the client path to real Behavior/Fact objects before any candidate question; also still open are the unchecked A1 fast path, A2 authority transitions, unread A4 membership and A6 durability, and the residual latency/ballot-range question for the explained Accept-reply candidate. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
